chunks: "RTL reuse means writing a block once, in a way that lets me drop it into many designs without rewriting it.

The main tools are parameters and generate statements, so one FIFO or synchronizer serves different widths and depths; packages and interfaces, so types and signal bundles are defined in one place; and standard interface protocols, like AXI or APB, so blocks plug together without glue logic.
It matters for three reasons. First, schedule: I don't want to redesign a UART or a DMA engine for every chip.
Second, quality: a block that's already been verified and used in silicon is far less risky than a fresh one, and verification is usually the biggest cost in a chip project.
Third, consistency across the team, one clock-domain-crossing cell, one reset synchronizer, one way of doing things. But reuse isn't free.
A reusable block needs a clean port list, parameters that are documented, lint and clock-domain checks passing, and a testbench that covers the configurations people will use.
If a block has twenty parameters, you can't verify every combination, so I'd limit the configuration space.
And I'd use parameters and generate rather than copy-paste and edit, since copies drift and bugs get fixed in one copy only."
